subQuestions.questionText:
Martha needs to buy school uniforms for her son and daughter. She compares the prices of three different stores as shown in TABLE 1 below.

**TABLE 1: COST OF SCHOOL UNIFORMS AT THREE DIFFERENT STORES**

| ITEMS | STORE A | STORE B | STORE C |
|---|---|---|---|
| White shirt | R110,00 for 2 | R44,99 each | R110,00 for 2 |
| Grey skirt | R163,00 for 2 | R54,99 each | R130,00 |
| Grey shorts | R186,00 | R39,99 | R99,95 |
| Grey school socks | R40,50 for 2 packs | R18,99 per pack | R89,99 for 3 packs |
| White school socks | R85,00 for 5 packs | R11,99 per pack | R85,99 for 5 packs |
| School shoes (girls) | R349,00 | R159,99 | R170,00 |
| School shoes (boys) | R318,00 | R169,99 | R275,00 |
| **TOTAL** | **P** | --- | --- |

NOTE: There are two pairs of socks in each pack.

Identify whether the prices given in TABLE 1 are numerical or categorical data.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marks 1 & 2: Numerical (2A correct classification)

Teaching point: Prices are counted/measured amounts, so they are numerical (quantitative) data. Categorical data would be labels such as the store name or the item name.

subQuestions.label: 1.1.6 (a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Martha compares the prices of school uniforms at THREE different stores: Store A, Store B and Store C.

The probability of selecting Store C to buy all the school items is 0,3333333333.

Define the term *probability* in the given context.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The chance / likelihood … (1A chance/likelihood)
Mark 2: … of selecting Store C (1A store C)

Full answer: "The chance (or likelihood) of selecting Store C to buy all the school items."

Teaching point: A definition "in the given context" must name the actual event — a general definition such as "how likely something is" on its own does not earn the second mark.

subQuestions.label: 1.1.6 (b)
subQuestions.questionText:
The probability of selecting Store C to buy all the school items is 0,3333333333.

Write down this probability as a percentage rounded to the nearest whole number.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $0{,}3333333333 \times 100\%$ (1MA calculating percentage)
Mark 2: $= 33{,}33333333\% = 33\%$ (1A rounded percentage)

Teaching point: To turn a decimal probability into a percentage, multiply by 100. "Nearest whole number" means no decimal places, so 33,33…% rounds down to 33%.

subQuestions.questionText:
One of the many investment options in South Africa is the stokvel option. TABLE 2 below shows two stokvel plans (Plan A and Plan B) over a 24-month period.

**TABLE 2: TWO STOKVEL PLANS (United African Stokvel)**

| | PLAN A (MONTHLY FIXED TERM PLAN) | PLAN B (ONCE-OFF SAVING PLAN) |
|---|---|---|
| Saving period | 24 months | 24 months |
| Amount saved | Monthly contributions: R2 500 | Once-off amount: R60 000 |
| Total amount at the end of 24 months | R74 286,84 | R92 065,71 |

Define *investment* in the given context.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: An investment is any form of saving that you put into a financial scheme, bank or stokvel … (1A form of savings)
Mark 2: … that will result in interest. (1A interest)

Teaching point: Both ideas are needed — money set aside (saved) AND a return/interest earned on it.

subQuestions.questionText:
TABLE 2 shows two stokvel plans over a 24-month period.

**TABLE 2: TWO STOKVEL PLANS**

| | PLAN A (MONTHLY FIXED TERM PLAN) | PLAN B (ONCE-OFF SAVING PLAN) |
|---|---|---|
| Saving period | 24 months | 24 months |
| Amount saved | Monthly contributions: R2 500 | Once-off amount: R60 000 |
| Total amount at the end of 24 months | R74 286,84 | R92 065,71 |

Calculate the total contributions for Plan A over the 24-month period.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\text{Total contributions} = \text{R}2\,500 \times 24$ (1MA multiply by months)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}60\,000$ (1A simplification)

Teaching point: Plan A pays the same amount every month, so the total paid in is the monthly amount multiplied by the number of months.

subQuestions.questionText:

The price of diesel in Gauteng in March 2022 was 1 955,28 c/ℓ (cents per litre).

Write this price in rand per litre. Round off your answer to the nearest R0,50.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $1\,955{,}28\ \text{c/ℓ} \div 100$ (1MA dividing by 100)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}19{,}55\text{/ℓ}$ (1A rand per litre)

subQuestions.questionText:
ANNEXURE A shows a summary of Bomvana's Car and Household Insurance Policy (BiWay.co.za).

**SUMMARY OF CAR AND HOUSEHOLD INSURANCE POLICY**

| | |
|---|---|
| Client Number | 22506623 |
| Policy Number | 23388350 |
| Commencement Date | 1 September 2013 |
| Statement Date | 30 August 2022 |
| Policyholder name | BOMVANA |

Write down the policy number of Bomvana's insurance policy.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marks 1 & 2: Policy number = 23388350 (2RT correct number)

Teaching point: Read carefully — the client number (22506623) and the policy number (23388350) are two different numbers on the same document.

subQuestions.questionText:
ANNEXURE A shows a summary of Bomvana's Car and Household Insurance Policy.

**SUMMARY OF COVER**

| Insured Items | Description | Premium |
|---|---|---|
| MiPersonal Accident | R25 000 | R7,16 |
| MiWheels – Car 1 | KIA PICANTO 1.1 LX -2004 | R200,41 |
| MiWheels – Car 2 | TOYOTA COROLLA 1.6 -2013 | R520,41 |
| MiWheels – Car 3 | FORD IKON 1.6i -2005 | R133,16 |
| MiWheels – Car 4 | VW POLO 1.0 TSI -2019 | **A** |
| MiHome Content | BOMVANA'S RESIDENTIAL ADDRESS | R201,79 |
| MiMovables | | R23,30 |
| RoadCover | | R9,07 |
| Total Discount | For having the above noted multiple insured items on cover | –R266,15 |
| **Total Monthly Premium (including 15% VAT)** | | **R2 184,21** |

Determine the missing value **A**, the monthly premium for the VW Polo.
subQuestions.memoText:
**Table values excluding A and the discount**

Mark 1: $\text{R}7{,}16 + \text{R}200{,}41 + \text{R}520{,}41 + \text{R}133{,}16 + \text{R}201{,}79 + \text{R}23{,}30 + \text{R}9{,}07$ (1MA adding all premiums)
$= \text{R}1\,095{,}30$

**Value of A**

Mark 2: $\text{R}2\,184{,}21 - \text{R}1\,095{,}30$ (1MCA subtracting from total premium)
Mark 3: $+\ \text{R}266{,}15$ (1MA adding the discount)
Mark 4: $A = \text{R}1\,355{,}06$ (1CA simplification)

**OR**

$\text{R}1\,095{,}30 + A + (-\text{R}266{,}15) = \text{R}2\,184{,}21$ (1MA adding all premiums)
$A = \text{R}2\,184{,}21 + \text{R}266{,}15 - \text{R}1\,095{,}30$ (1MCA subtracting from total premium; 1MA adding the discount)
$= \text{R}1\,355{,}06$ (1CA simplification)

**OR**

$(\text{R}7{,}16 + \text{R}200{,}41 + \text{R}520{,}41 + \text{R}133{,}16 + \text{R}201{,}79 + \text{R}23{,}30 + \text{R}9{,}07) - \text{R}266{,}15$ (1MA adding all premiums; 1MA subtracting the discount)
$= \text{R}829{,}15$
$A = \text{R}2\,184{,}21 - \text{R}829{,}15$ (1MCA subtracting from total premium)
$= \text{R}1\,355{,}06$ (1CA simplification)

Teaching point: The discount is a negative amount on the statement, so when you work backwards to find a missing premium you must ADD the discount back.

subQuestions.questionText:
Bomvana's insurance statement shows a Total Discount of –R266,15 and a Total Monthly Premium (including 15% VAT) of R2 184,21.

Bomvana qualifies for a discount on his insurance premiums as he has insured many items.

Calculate the percentage discount that he receives if the total monthly premium before the discount was R2 450,36.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: numerator R266,15 (1RT correct amount)
Mark 2: $\text{Percentage discount} = \dfrac{\text{R}266{,}15}{\text{R}2\,450{,}36} \times 100\%$ (1MA correct %-calculation)
Mark 3: $= 10{,}86\%$ (1CA simplification)

**OR**

$\%\ \text{discount} = \dfrac{\text{R}2\,450{,}36 - \text{R}2\,184{,}21}{\text{R}2\,450{,}36} \times 100\%$ (1RT correct amount; 1MA correct %-calculation)
$= 10{,}86\%$ (1CA simplification)

**OR**

$\text{Percentage discount} = 100\% - \left(\dfrac{\text{R}2\,184{,}21}{\text{R}2\,450{,}36} \times 100\%\right)$ (1RT correct amount)
$= 100\% - 89{,}14\%$ (1MA correct %-calculation)
$= 10{,}86\%$ (1CA simplification)

NPR (no penalty for correct rounding).

Teaching point: A percentage discount is always calculated on the price BEFORE the discount (R2 450,36), not on the discounted price.

subQuestions.questionText:
Bomvana's insurance policy shows the following excess values (the excess is the amount payable by YOU to the service provider whenever you make a claim):

| Claim event | Excess |
|---|---|
| Accident and Intentional Damage | R7 000,00 |
| Theft and Hijacking | R7 000,00 |
| Window glass only claim (not glass forming part of roof) | R1 490,00 |
| Earthquake, Storm, Hail, Flood and Snow | R7 000,00 |
| Fire and Explosion | R7 000,00 |

Bomvana was involved in a motor vehicle accident during July 2022. The quotation for damages from the panel beaters was R43 520,00.

Determine the amount the insurance company will pay the panel beaters.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\text{Claim amount} = \text{R}43\,520 - \text{R}7\,000$ (1RT identifying R7 000)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}36\,520$ (1A claim amount)

Teaching point: The accident excess of R7 000 is paid by the policyholder, so the insurer pays the quotation less the excess.

subQuestions.questionText:
Bomvana's insurance statement shows a Total Monthly Premium of R2 184,21, which includes 15% VAT.

Calculate the amount of VAT included in the total monthly premium.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\dfrac{15}{115}$ (1A correct VAT calculation)
Mark 2: $\text{VAT} = \dfrac{15}{115} \times \dfrac{\text{R}2\,184{,}21}{1}$ (1MA multiplying)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}284{,}90$ (1A simplification)

**OR**

$\text{Amount before VAT} = \dfrac{\text{R}2\,184{,}21}{1{,}15}$ (1MA dividing by 1,15)
$= \text{R}1\,899{,}31$ (1A VAT-excluded amount)
$\text{VAT amount} = \text{R}2\,184{,}21 - \text{R}1\,899{,}31 = \text{R}284{,}90$ (1A simplification)

Teaching point: When an amount already INCLUDES VAT, the VAT portion is $\dfrac{15}{115}$ of that amount, not 15% of it.

subQuestions.questionText:
Bomvana's insurance policy covers four vehicles:

| Vehicle | Monthly premium |
|---|---|
| KIA PICANTO 1.1 LX -2004 | R200,41 |
| TOYOTA COROLLA 1.6 -2013 | R520,41 |
| FORD IKON 1.6i -2005 | R133,16 |
| VW POLO 1.0 TSI -2019 | R1 355,06 |

The premium for the Toyota Corolla is much lower than that of the VW Polo.

Give ONE possible reason for this big difference in the premium amount.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marks 1 & 2: Any ONE valid reason (2O correct explanation), for example:
• The VW Polo costs more than the Toyota Corolla.
• The Toyota is an older model (2013) and the VW is a newer model (2019).
• The retail value of the VW Polo is higher, therefore the replacement value is higher.
• The VW is a high-risk vehicle (more often stolen/hijacked).
• The primary driver of the VW is a younger, less experienced driver.

Teaching point: Insurance premiums track the cost of replacing or repairing the vehicle and the risk of a claim — newer, more expensive and more frequently stolen cars cost more to insure.

subQuestions.questionText:
Bomvana pays a MiHome premium of R201,79 per month for household content cover to the value of R200 000. After the household contents were evaluated for insurance purposes, he bought an additional lounge suite.

Explain how the purchase of this new item will affect his MiHome content premium.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marks 1 & 2: His premium will increase, as his household content value will increase to more than R200 000. (2O valid conclusion)

Teaching point: Household content cover is based on the total replacement value of everything in the home. Adding an item raises that value, so the cover — and therefore the premium — must go up.

subQuestions.questionText:
The sanitation tariffs for Johannesburg and Cape Town are presented in TABLE 3. Johannesburg uses the area of a property to determine the sanitation bill. Cape Town uses a percentage of the total water usage to determine the sanitation bill (the same way as they calculate the water bill).

**TABLE 3 (part): JOHANNESBURG SANITATION TARIFFS – DOMESTIC (VAT excl.)**

| Property size | Tariff |
|---|---|
| Up to and including 300 m² | R228,06 |
| Larger than 300 m² to 1 000 m² | R443,96 |
| Larger than 1 000 m² to 2 000 m² | R671,63 |
| Larger than 2 000 m² | R967,71 |

NOTE: Sanitation refers to waste water that is drained from a household.

Write down, to the nearest ten cents and excluding VAT, the cost for sanitation in Johannesburg if a property is 175 m².
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\text{Cost of sanitation} = \text{R}228{,}06$ (1RT correct amount)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}228{,}10$ (1R correct rounding)

Answer only: full marks.

Teaching point: 175 m² falls in the "up to and including 300 m²" bracket. "Nearest ten cents" means the answer must end in a whole number of ten-cent units, so R228,06 becomes R228,10.

subQuestions.questionText:
Cape Town uses a percentage of the total water usage to determine the sanitation bill.

**TABLE 3 (part): CAPE TOWN SANITATION TARIFFS – DOMESTIC (VAT incl.)**

| Usage | Tariff | Increase from previous |
|---|---|---|
| 0–4,2 kℓ | R16,03 per kℓ | R0,66 increase per kℓ |
| 4,2–7,35 kℓ | R22,02 per kℓ | R0,91 increase per kℓ |
| 7,35–24,5 kℓ | R30,92 per kℓ | R1,28 increase per kℓ |
| 24,5–35 kℓ | R48,65 per kℓ | R2,01 increase per kℓ |

Calculate the cost for 4,1 kℓ sanitation in Cape Town before the increase.
subQuestions.memoText:
**Tariff before the increase**

Mark 1: $\text{R}16{,}03 - \text{R}0{,}66$ (1RT reading from table)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}15{,}37$ (1A simplification)

**Cost of sanitation**

Mark 3: $4{,}1\ \text{kℓ} \times \text{R}15{,}37$ (1MCA multiply by tariff)
Mark 4: $= \text{R}63{,}02$ (1CA simplification)

**OR**

Amount after increase $= \text{R}16{,}03 \times 4{,}1\ \text{kℓ} = \text{R}65{,}723$ (1A simplification)
Increase $= \text{R}0{,}66 \times 4{,}1\ \text{kℓ} = \text{R}2{,}706$ (1RT reading from table)
Amount before increase $= \text{R}65{,}723 - \text{R}2{,}706$ (1MCA multiply by tariff)
$= \text{R}63{,}02$ (1CA simplification)

Teaching point: The "increase from previous" column tells you how much the tariff went UP, so the old tariff is the current tariff minus that increase.

Marks 1 & 2: (1MA all three correct kℓ amounts; 1RT three correct tariffs)
$4{,}2\ \text{kℓ} \times \text{R}16{,}03 = \text{R}67{,}33$
$3{,}15\ \text{kℓ} \times \text{R}22{,}02 = \text{R}69{,}36$
$14{,}65\ \text{kℓ} \times \text{R}30{,}92 = \text{R}452{,}98$
Mark 3: Total $= \text{R}589{,}67$ (1CA finding total sanitation bill)

**Sanitation Bill – Johannesburg: Mr Jones** (550 m² falls in the R443,96 bracket, VAT excl.)

Mark 4: $\text{VAT} = \text{R}443{,}96 \times \dfrac{15}{100} = \text{R}66{,}59$ (1RT correct amount)
Marks 5 & 6: $\text{Total amount} = \text{R}443{,}96 + \text{R}66{,}59 = \text{R}510{,}55$ (1MCA adding values; 1CA simplification)

**Difference in sanitation bill**

Marks 7 & 8: $\text{R}589{,}67 - \text{R}510{,}55 = \text{R}79{,}12$ (1MCA subtracting values; 1CA simplification)

Teaching point: Cape Town's tariff is a sliding scale — only the kilolitres inside each band are charged at that band's rate ($4{,}2$; then $7{,}35-4{,}2=3{,}15$; then $22-7{,}35=14{,}65$). Johannesburg's tariff is a flat amount for the property size, but it excludes VAT, so 15% must be added before the two bills can be compared.

subQuestions.questionText:
Johannesburg charges a FIXED sanitation amount based on the size of the property (for example R228,06 for a property up to 300 m² and R443,96 for a property larger than 300 m² up to 1 000 m²), regardless of how much water is used. Cape Town charges according to the amount of water used on a sliding scale.

Explain how the tariff system used in Johannesburg is beneficial to home owners in terms of water usage.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marks 1 & 2: Any ONE valid explanation (2O correct explanation), for example:
• The fixed rate allows you to use as much water as you can for the same amount.
• It benefits home owners with smaller properties, who pay less.
• Even if water usage varies from month to month, the cost/bill remains the same amount.

Teaching point: A fixed tariff removes the link between usage and cost, so the bill is predictable no matter how much water is used.

subQuestions.questionText:

subQuestions.questionText:
The number of unemployed people in South Africa in Quarter 2 of 2021 was 7,6 million.

The unemployment rate for Quarter 2 was 34,4%.

Determine the number of people employed in South Africa during Quarter 2.
subQuestions.memoText:
**Total number of people (labour force)**

Mark 1: $\dfrac{100}{34{,}4} \times 7{,}6\ \text{million}$ (1RT correct percentage)
Mark 2: $= 22\,093\,023{,}26 \approx 22\,093\,023$ (1A simplification)

**Number of employed people**

Mark 3: $= 22\,093\,023 - 7\,600\,000$ (1MCA subtracting values)

$= 14\,493\,023$ (1CA total number of people)

NPR (no penalty for correct rounding).

Teaching point: The 34,4% rate applies to the whole labour force. Find the labour force first (7,6 million is 34,4% of it), then subtract the unemployed to get the employed.

questions.title: Personal income tax and the best-selling vehicles in three countries

subQuestions.questionText:
Mr Louw, aged 53, earned an annual taxable income of R495 602 for the year ending 28 February 2022. He does not contribute to any medical aid.

The following formula can be used to calculate annual tax payable before the rebate:

**Annual Tax Payable before the rebate = R115 762 + [36% × (annual taxable income – 488 700)]**

Use this formula to calculate Mr Louw's annual tax payable before the rebate.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\text{Tax payable} = \text{R}115\,762 + \left[\dfrac{36}{100} \times (495\,602 - 488\,700)\right]$ (1SF substituting value)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}115\,762 + \text{R}2\,484{,}72$ (1MA adding values)
Mark 3: $= \text{R}118\,246{,}72$ (1CA simplification)

NPR (no penalty for correct rounding). Answer only: full marks.

Teaching point: Work inside the brackets first — only the income ABOVE R488 700 is taxed at 36%; the R115 762 is the fixed tax on the income below that threshold.

subQuestions.questionText:
Mr Louw, aged 53, earned an annual taxable income of R495 602 for the year ending 28 February 2022. His annual tax payable before the rebate is R118 246,72.

Mr Louw feels that the monthly tax table is an easier option for him to calculate his monthly tax payable. TABLE 5 below shows the monthly deductions for three income categories for the year ending 28 February 2022.

**TABLE 5: MONTHLY DEDUCTION TAX TABLE FOR THREE INCOME CATEGORIES FOR THE YEAR ENDING 28 FEBRUARY 2022**

| Monthly Income | Under 65 | 65–74 | Over 75 |
|---|---|---|---|
| R41 241–R41 291 | R8 473 | R7 723 | R7 473 |
| R41 292–R41 342 | R8 491 | R7 741 | R7 491 |
| R41 343–R41 393 | R8 510 | R7 760 | R7 510 |

The monthly rebate for a person younger than 65 years old is R1 368,75.

Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his monthly tax will be correct according to the monthly deduction table.
subQuestions.memoText:
Consistent accuracy from QUESTION 4.1.1.

**Monthly tax (before rebate)**

Mark 1: $= \text{R}118\,246{,}72 \div 12$ (1MA dividing by 12)
Mark 2: $= \text{R}9\,853{,}89$ (1A monthly tax)

**After rebate**

Mark 3: $= \text{R}9\,853{,}89 - \text{R}1\,368{,}75$ (1MA subtracting rebate)
Mark 4: $= \text{R}8\,485{,}14$ (1MCA finding tax after rebate)

**Monthly taxable income**

Mark 5: $= \text{R}495\,602 \div 12 = \text{R}41\,300{,}17$ (1A monthly income)

**Tax payable according to TABLE 5** (R41 300,17 falls in the R41 292–R41 342 bracket, Under 65) $= \text{R}8\,491$

Mark 6: He is incorrect. (1O conclusion) — R8 485,14 ≠ R8 491

**OR**

Annual rebate $= \text{R}1\,368{,}75 \times 12$ (1MA multiplying by 12) $= \text{R}16\,425$ (1A correct annual rebate)
Annual tax (after rebate) $= \text{R}118\,246{,}72 - \text{R}16\,425 = \text{R}101\,821{,}72$ (1A annual tax)
Monthly income $= \text{R}495\,602 \div 12 = \text{R}41\,300{,}17$ (1A monthly income)
Annual tax from the table $= \text{R}8\,491 \times 12 = \text{R}101\,892$ (1MCA annual tax)
He is incorrect. (1O conclusion)

**OR**

Monthly tax before rebate $= \text{R}118\,246{,}72 \div 12$ (1MA dividing by 12) $= \text{R}9\,853{,}89$ (1A correct answer)
Monthly taxable income $= \text{R}495\,602 \div 12 = \text{R}41\,300{,}17$ (1A correct answer)
From the table, before rebate $= \text{R}8\,491 + \text{R}1\,368{,}75$ (1MA adding rebate) $= \text{R}9\,859{,}75$ (1MCA finding tax before rebate)
He is incorrect. (1O conclusion)

Teaching point: The table already gives tax AFTER the rebate, so you must compare like with like — either take the rebate off your calculated figure, or add it back to the table figure.

subQuestions.questionText:
**TABLE 5: MONTHLY DEDUCTION TAX TABLE FOR THREE INCOME CATEGORIES FOR THE YEAR ENDING 28 FEBRUARY 2022**

subQuestions.questionText:
The interquartile range for the top 10 vehicles sold in South Africa is 7 669 and the value of Quartile 1 is 11 408.

Calculate the value of Quartile 3.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$ (1A correct formula)
Mark 2: $7\,669 = Q_3 - 11\,408$ (1SF substituting into formula)
Mark 3: $Q_3 = 7\,669 + 11\,408$ (1MA changing the subject of the formula)
Mark 4: $= 19\,077$ (1CA simplification)

Answer only: full marks.

Teaching point: The interquartile range is the "spread of the middle half" — the distance from Quartile 1 to Quartile 3. Rearrange the formula to make $Q_3$ the subject.

subQuestions.questionText:
The inflation rate in America for 2021 was 7% and in 2020 it was 1,4%. The price of a Ford F-series vehicle in 2022 is $32 332.

It is stated that the price of the Ford F-series vehicle in 2020 was more than $29 800.

Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether this statement is valid.
subQuestions.memoText:
**2020 price of the Ford F-series** (removing the 2021 inflation of 7%)

Mark 1: numerator 100 (1RT numerator)
Mark 2: denominator 107 (1RT denominator)
$\$32\,332 \times \dfrac{100}{107}$
Mark 3: $= \$30\,216{,}82$ (1A 2020 price)

**2019 price of the Ford F-series** (removing the 2020 inflation of 1,4%)

Mark 4: $\$30\,216{,}82 \times \dfrac{100}{101{,}4}$ (1MA concept of % decrease)
Mark 5: $= \$29\,799{,}63$ (1CA simplification)

Mark 6: The statement is NOT valid. (1O not valid)

**OR**

$\$32\,332 \times \dfrac{100}{107} \times \dfrac{100}{101{,}4}$ (1RT numerator; 1RT denominator; 1RT numerator; 1RT denominator)
$= \$29\,799{,}63$ (1CA simplification)
The statement is not valid. (1O not valid)

Teaching point: To work BACKWARDS from a price that already includes inflation, divide by $(100 + \text{rate})$ and multiply by 100 — do not simply subtract the percentage. $\$29\,799{,}63$ is less than $\$29\,800$, so the claim fails (by only 37 cents).

subQuestions.questionText:
ANNEXURE B shows the five best-selling vehicles in America for 2021. The **TOTAL NUMBER OF VEHICLES SOLD = 2 584 176**.

| Vehicle | Number sold |
|---|---|

| Chev Silverado | 519 774 |

Determine, as a percentage, the probability of purchasing a Ram Pickup in America.

Mark 2: denominator 2 584 176 (1RT correct denominator)
$\text{Probability} = \dfrac{569\,388}{2\,584\,176} \times 100\%$
Mark 3: $= 22{,}03\%$ (1CA simplification)

NPR (no penalty for correct rounding).

Teaching point: Probability as a percentage = (favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes) × 100. The "total" here is the total of all five best-selling vehicles, 2 584 176.

subQuestions.questionText:
A line graph titled 'CONTRIBUTIONS OF THREE PROVINCES TO THE COUNTRY'S GROWTH' plots each province's percentage contribution to four sectors. Readings from the graph:

The total amount contributed by the three provinces to agriculture was R8,3 billion. Determine which part of this amount Western Cape contributed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: reading $3\% + 4\% + 4\%$ (1RT all 3 values)
Mark 2: $= 11\%$ (1A simplification)
Mark 3: $\dfrac{4}{11} \times \text{R}8\,300\,000\,000$ (1MCA calculating ratio)
Mark 4: $= \text{R}3\,018\,181\,818$ / R3,018181818 billion (1CA simplification)

**OR**

Total contribution $= \dfrac{100}{11} \times \text{R}8\,300\,000\,000$ (1RT correct values)
$= \text{R}75\,454\,545\,454$ (1A simplification)
WC contribution $= \dfrac{4}{100} \times \text{R}75\,454\,545\,454$ (1MCA calculating ratio)
$= \text{R}3\,018\,181\,818$ (1CA simplification)

NPR (no penalty for correct rounding).

Teaching point: The three percentages (3% + 4% + 4% = 11%) make up the whole R8,3 billion, so the Western Cape's share is 4 out of those 11 parts — not 4% of R8,3 billion.

Identify the currency which is the weakest against the rand.
subQuestions.memoText:

Teaching point: The weakest currency is the one where ONE unit is worth the least in rand — the yen is worth only R0,12565 per unit, less than the rouble (R0,143373) and far less than the others.

Show how the Russian rouble of 0,143373 ZAR per unit was determined.
subQuestions.memoText:

Mark 2: denominator 6,97481 (1A denominator)

Teaching point: The two columns are reciprocals of each other. If R1 buys 6,97481 roubles, then 1 rouble buys $\dfrac{1}{6{,}97481}$ rand.

Give ONE reason why you would motivate Ryan to invest in a Canadian company.
subQuestions.memoText:

• To diversify his income (spread his risk across countries).
• The Canadian currency is stronger than the rand.
• He will get a better return on his investment.

Teaching point: Investing offshore in a stronger currency protects value if the rand weakens, and spreads risk across more than one economy.

subQuestions.questionText:
Ryan invested R1 230 000 in shares in a Canadian company. After 2 years and 8 months, Ryan sold his shares and received a final amount of R1 529 360.

In South Africa Ryan would have received an interest rate of 8,1%, compounded annually, for 2 years and 8 months.

Ryan stated that he earned more than R14 000 return on his foreign investment compared to a potential South African investment.

Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether Ryan's statement is valid.
subQuestions.memoText:
**Year 1**

Mark 1: $\text{R}1\,230\,000 \times \dfrac{8{,}1}{100}$ (1MA calculating 8,1%)
$= \text{R}99\,630$
Mark 2: Total after year 1 $= \text{R}1\,230\,000 + \text{R}99\,630 = \text{R}1\,329\,630$ (1A interest year 1 / amount end year 1)

**Year 2**

$\text{R}1\,329\,630 \times \dfrac{8{,}1}{100} = \text{R}107\,700{,}03$
Mark 3: Total after year 2 $= \text{R}1\,329\,630 + \text{R}107\,700{,}03 = \text{R}1\,437\,330{,}03$ (1CA amount year 2)

**8 months**

Mark 4: $\text{R}1\,437\,330{,}03 \times \dfrac{8{,}1}{100} \times \dfrac{8}{12}$ (1MA calculating 8 months)
$= \text{R}77\,615{,}82162$

Mark 5: Final amount $= \text{R}1\,437\,330{,}03 + \text{R}77\,615{,}82162 = \text{R}1\,514\,945{,}852$ (1CA final amount)

Mark 6 & 7: $\text{R}1\,529\,360 - \text{R}1\,514\,945{,}852 = \text{R}14\,414{,}15$ (1CA difference)

Mark 8: His statement is valid. (1O conclusion) — R14 414,15 is more than R14 000.

**OR**

Total year 1 $= \text{R}1\,230\,000 \times 1{,}081$ (1A calculating 1,081; 1MCA multiplying with 1,081) $= \text{R}1\,329\,630$ (1A amount end year 1)
Total year 2 $= \text{R}1\,329\,630 \times 1{,}081 = \text{R}1\,437\,330{,}03$ (1CA amount end year 2)
Interest rate for 8 months $= 8{,}1\% \times 8 \div 12 = 5{,}4\%$ (1A calculating 5,4%)
Total after 2 years 8 months $= \text{R}1\,437\,330{,}03 \times 1{,}054 = \text{R}1\,514\,945{,}85$ (1CA final amount)
Difference $= \text{R}1\,529\,360 - \text{R}1\,514\,945{,}85 = \text{R}14\,414{,}15$ (1CA difference)
The statement is valid. (1O conclusion)

NPR (no penalty for correct rounding).

Teaching point: "Compounded annually" means the interest for year 2 is worked out on the year-1 closing balance, not on the original R1 230 000. The final 8 months is a part-year, so the annual rate is scaled by $\dfrac{8}{12}$.
